title: Preserving National History Locally: Tour of the Petaluma Woman’s Club
location: Petaluma Woman’s Club, 518 B Street, Petaluma, CA, 94952, United States
description:
Celebrate the Petaluma Woman’s Club’s recent addition to the National Register of Historic Places.
Date:  Wednesday May 27, 5:00-6:30 PM
Venue: Petaluma Woman’s Club
518 B Street
Petaluma, CA 94952
Cost:  Free
Please RSVP Here

As a part of National Historic Preservation Month festivities, the Petaluma Woman’s Club invites you to a special event in celebration of its recent designation on the National Register of Historic Places. The program will feature a presentation by local historians and current Club members on the history of the Petaluma Woman’s Club, including its role in the broader Women’s Club movement. The presentation will be followed by a guided tour of the historic 1913 Craftsman-style building, designed by notable local architect Brainerd Jones.

title: Wednesday Night Walk: Petaluma Downtown & Riverfront
description:
"SONOMA COUNTY OUTDOORS"
Wednesday Night Walk: Petaluma Downtown and Riverfront

* Want to walk for fitness and exercise?
* New to walking and want to build up stamina?
* Like a slower pace than our Tuesday Night Fitness Hike?
* Would walking with a committed group of walkers help you?

If you said yes to any of these, then the Wednesday Night Walk in Petaluma is for you. We start at Aqus Cafe and take in the West Side of town, including some of Downtown, the Waterfront and a few of the Historic home of old Petaluma. We walk about 3-1/2 to 4-1/2 miles depending on weather conditions and the pace of the group that night.

Afterward if you have the time, join us at Aqus Cafe for a bite to eat and some liquid refreshment before heading home. Aqus Cafe is a true gem of a gathering place, restaurant, coffee house, and live music venue. But it's the people on either side of the counter that make this place so special.

DETAILS:

* Meetup time: 6:00pm (we hike at 6:10 sharp)
* Meetup location: Aqus Cafe
* Distance: 3.5 to 4-1/2 miles
* Duration: 75-80 minutes
* Pace: Easy/Moderate (about 2.5-3 mph or 20-24 minute miles)
* Difficulty: Easy (if you've walked 3-4 miles recently)
* Hills: Mostly flat with a few small and easy to climb hills
* Optional After-Hike Gathering at Aqus Cafe

WHAT TO BRING:

* A good pair of walking shoes
* Water (you'll be glad you did)
* A fun attitude!

SO HOW FAST ARE WE WALKING?
The Wednesday Night Walk is about 2.5 - 3 mph (20-24 minute miles)
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike is about 3.5-4 mph (15-17 minute miles)

HOW DO YOU PARTICIPATE?
Sign up with Meetup and RSVP Today! This also gets you on our email list to make you aware of upcoming events, hikes and walks. You will not be spammed. If you are, let me know. Spamming will not be tolerated.

WHY DO YOU NEED TO RSVP?
It's important to RSVP for these walks. When all the people have arrived for a walk that have RSVP'd, we leave... it might mean we leave early. If you didn't RSVP we are not going to wait for you. Plus, it's just a nice courtesy to the organizer and other participants. Please take the time to RSVP.

QUESTIONS?
Email me with any questions by using the "Contact Us" link on the left hand side bar of this meetup group page.

Hope to see you on a walk or hike soon!

Gary
SCO Organizer

title: Happy Hour Crafts
description:
The Rebel Craft Collective
Wine + tasty snacks + your latest project and a friendly group of likeminded crafters... what better way to unwind? Come join us!

This is a relaxed, drop-in-friendly event. Come when you can, leave when you must. Newcomers and occasional-comers are always welcome!

**What do we mean by “crafts”?**
Whatever “craft” means to you! And whatever is portable enough to bring to a wine bar. Knitting, crochet, and other fiber arts are most common, but we have also warmly welcomed people who sketch, color, embroider, bead, and more. If your craft isn’t portable, we will happily ooh and aah over photos of your work-in-progress, or chat about your plans for your next project.

**Health & Safety**
Masks are very welcome, and nobody will pressure you to eat or drink. If the weather is nice, we will try to sit outside. If you aren’t eating/drinking during the event, please consider ordering some of La Dolce Vita’s delicious food to-go, in order to help support our gracious, long-time venue.

**Parking**
Parking in downtown Petaluma is free, but street parking has a strictly enforced 2 hour limit until 6pm. To park for longer, try the nearest garage:

* The Second Street Garage entrance is located on C Street between First and Second Streets. It's all day parking on every level and a short walk to La Dolce Vita.

**Ages**
It's a wine bar, so this event is for adult crafters (though you're certainly not required to drink wine!). We’re okay with babes-in-arms if you are, but this is not the right setting for wee crafters who are moving about on their own.

title: From Past to Future: Stewarding Our Wetlands Together
location: Petaluma Historical Library & Museum, 20 4th St, Petaluma, CA, United States
description:
Join us for an engaging panel discussion with conservation leaders and community partners working across the Petaluma River watershed.
Date:  Thursday May 28 6:00 – 7:30 pm
Venue: Petaluma Historical Library & Museum
20 4th Street (Corner of 4th & B St.)
Petaluma, CA 94952
Free!  Reservations Appreciated
How have our relationships with Petaluma’s wetlands changed over time—and what does stewardship look like in a changing climate?
Join us for an engaging panel discussion connected to Time & Tide: An Artful Exploration of Petaluma’s Wetlands, bringing together conservation leaders and community partners working across the Petaluma River watershed.
Together, we’ll explore how this landscape has been shaped by both human activity and natural processes, and how today’s efforts—grounded in restoration science, Indigenous knowledge, and community action—are helping to build a more resilient future.
Panelists will share insights on:

The historical transformation of the watershed
Current restoration and conservation efforts
The role of collaboration and community stewardship
How wetlands support climate resilience—reducing flood risk, supporting biodiversity, and helping our region adapt to rising seas

This conversation invites us to reflect on what it means to learn from the past, act in the present, and steward the wetlands we all depend on for the future.
Free! RSVPS appreciated.

Though we launch from the heart of downtown, the central turning basin offers a surprisingly serene setting—calm water, open sky, and a sense of ease that feels far removed from daily life. This all-levels, 90-minute session is designed for everyone: experienced yogis, seasoned paddle boarders, and complete beginners alike. title: Plein Air Paint Out
location: Ellis Creek Water Recycling Facility, 3890 Cypress Drive, Petaluma, PA, 19454, United States
description:
A relaxed and inspiring morning of outdoor painting at one of Petaluma’s most beautiful wetland landscapes.

Saturday, May 31 8:00am – 12:00 pm

Please Make Your Reservations Here

Held in connection with the Petaluma Museum’s exhibitTime & Tide: An Artful Exploration of Petaluma’s Wetlands, this community paint out invites artists of all levels—from beginners to experienced plein air painters—to gather, observe, and create in the open air.
Painting outdoors—en plein air—offers a unique way to connect with the landscape. At Ellis Creek, you’ll experience shifting light, birdlife, and the quiet movement of water while capturing the wetlands through your own creative lens.
Whether you’re trying plein air painting for the first time or are a seasoned artist, this is a welcoming, low-pressure opportunity to slow down, observe, and create in community.
Good to Know:
Morning light is ideal, and we recommend arriving between 8:00–9:00 AM, with painting continuing through noon.
Ellis Creek offers free parking, restrooms, scenic views right from the lot, and easy access to painting spots near the ponds and along the trails.
The parking lot for the Ellis Creek Water Recycling Facility is close to 3882 Cypress Dr. Petaluma, CA 94954. GPS Coordinates: The main parking lot is at 38 13 35N, 122 35 08W approximately.
Guided instruction is not provided, but there will be opportunities for informal guidance, tips, and shared learning from fellow painters throughout the morning.
What to Bring:
A simple plein air kit might include:

Portable easel (French easel or pochade box)
Painting surface (8×10″ or 9×12″ panels or watercolor block)
Paint (oils, acrylics, or watercolor)
Brushes and/or palette knife
Water or solvent container (with lid)
Pencil for sketching
Paper towels or rags
Folding chair or stool
Sun protection (hat, sunscreen, umbrella)
Drinking water

Optional:

Wet panel carrier or wax paper for transport
Spray bottle (acrylics) or masking tape (watercolor)

title: Mindfulness Sunday Meditation: Cultivating Consciousness
description:
Meditate with a Monk in Sonoma County
Join us for a transformative workshop on mindfulness meditation and cultivating consciousness. Dive deep into the teachings of Theravada Buddhism, focusing on insight meditation to develop a clear understanding of the nature of the mind and consciousness. This workshop will include guided meditation sessions to help you strengthen your meditation practice and cultivate mindfulness in your daily life. Whether you are a beginner or an experienced meditator, this workshop offers a welcoming space to explore the depths of your own consciousness and enhance your spiritual journey. Come together with like-minded individuals to deepen your practice and connect with the wisdom of Theravada Buddhism, and provide an opportunity to deepen mindfulness, wisdom, and inner stillness.
Our sessions are led by Bhikkhunis closely associated with our Dhammadharini Sangha. Check out the [recording from the past event](https://youtube.com/live/s07U2kzWoWk?feature=share) on our YouTube channel.
You’re also welcome to join us in person at Dhammadharini Monastery, in the peaceful setting of our outdoor Dana Sala Pavilion

title: Sunday Funday SUP Paddle
location: The Floathouse Petaluma, 50 Water Street, Petaluma, CA, 94952
description: Sunday Funday SUP Paddle Lazy Sunday mornings and a little time on the river—what could be better? title: Tuesday Night Fitness Hike: 5+ Fast Miles, Downtown Petaluma and Western Hills
description:
"SONOMA COUNTY OUTDOORS"
WARNING: THE TUESDAY NIGHT FITNESS HIKE IS AN AEROBIC, FAST-PACED URBAN HIKE! WE TARGET A PACE OF 16-MINUTES PER MILE WITH ONLY BRIEF STOPS (TO REGROUP AS NEEDED). OUR SUMMER ROUTE INCLUDES THE HILLS IN HELEN PUTNAM PARK (740 FT. ELEVATION GAIN), AND OUR WINTER ROUTE EXPLORES THE WATER TANKS (690 FT. ELEVATION GAIN). IF YOU FIND YOU ARE HAVING DIFFICULTY KEEPING UP WITH THE LEADERS IN THIS GROUP, PLEASE USE THE OPT-OUT POINT AT THE FIRST MILE OF THE HIKE! ANOTHER OPTION IS OUR WEDNESDAY NIGHT WALK FOR A MORE MODERATE PACE. THANK YOU FOR HELPING ME KEEP THIS HIKE AN AEROBIC WORKOUT!

NOTE:
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike is posted on the SCO Calendar every week. Steve Tubbs is shown as the host each week but he might, or might not, show up to the event. This is, more often than not, a small group of regular, fit walkers who show up on time every Tuesday night to enjoy this rigorous walk. We leave promptly at 6:10 pm from the Kentucky Street entrance to the LanMart Building. So, if you don't see Steve on the Tuesday night you are there, you might see him on the next one.

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike, 5+ miles fast paced urban hike:

This Fitness Hike includes multiple steep uphill portions in Helen Putnam Park (during Daylight Savings Time), and at the Petaluma Water Tanks (after Daylight Savings Time ends).

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike:

* Warning! This is a FAST hike... a real workout!
* 5+ miles
* Meetup time 6:00 pm (We hike at 6:10 sharp)
* Difficulty is STRENUOUS!
* 90 minutes

This is a fast, evening Fitness Hike that starts downtown outside (on the sidewalk) of the LanMart Building (Brixx Restaurant, Heebe Jeebe) on Kentucky Street. We head west to Helen Putnam Park (or the Petaluma Water Tanks when DST ends) for some beautiful vistas before returning to our starting point on Kentucky Street. This hike is generally the same route and is focused primarily on fitness.

WHAT TO BRING:

* A good pair of walking/hiking shoes
* Water (you'll be glad you did)
* A fun attitude!

WHAT ABOUT THE DARKNESS?
Bring a SMALL flashlight. The sidewalks can be treacherous in west Petaluma, and you'll want to see those crags, cracks and upheavals in the concrete. Reflective clothing is also recommended so that vehicles can see you!

SO HOW FAST ARE WE WALKING?
The Wednesday Night Walk is about 2.5 mph (22 - 23 minute miles)
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike nearly 3.5 - 4.0 mph (we target a 16 minute mile, with multiple hills!)

HOW DO YOU PARTICIPATE?
Sign up with Meetup and RSVP Today! This also gets you on our email list to make you aware of upcoming events, hikes and walks.

WHY DO YOU NEED TO RSVP?

Please take the time to RSVP YES when you plan on attending an event. It is equally important to keep your RSVP up to date. If you've RSVP'd YES for an event, we are going to wait for you until the departure time. We leave promptly at 6:10 PM, so if you arrive late you can join us along the route. We typically hike the same route for each hike, and our focus is on aerobic exercise.

QUESTIONS?
Email me with any questions by using the "Contact Us" link on the left hand side bar of this meetup group page.

Hope to see you on a walk or hike soon!

SCO Organizers

title: UPDATE: 1st Wednesday! Wednesday Night Walk start at STARBUCKS  on the East Side
description:
"SONOMA COUNTY OUTDOORS"
Wednesday Night Walk: Petaluma East Side Green Belt

* Want to walk for fitness and exercise?
* New to walking and want to build up stamina?
* Like a slower pace than our Tuesday Night Fitness Hike?
* Would walking with a committed group of walkers help you?

If you said yes to any of these, then the Wednesday Night Walk in Petaluma is for you. We start at STARBUCKS at the leghorn shopping center, and walk about 4-1/2 miles depending on weather conditions and the pace of the group that night.

DETAILS:

* Meetup time: 6:00pm (we walk at 6:10 sharp)
* Meetup location: STARBUCKS
* Distance: \~ 4.5 miles
* Duration: 75-80 minutes
* Pace: Easy/Moderate (about 2.5-3 mph or 20-24 minute miles)
* Difficulty: Easy (if you've walked 3-4 miles recently)
* Hills: Mostly flat
* Optional After-walk gathering at
* WHAT TO BRING:
* A good pair of walking shoes
* Water (you'll be glad you did)
* A fun attitude!

SO HOW FAST ARE WE WALKING?
The Wednesday Night Walk is about 2.5 - 3 mph (20-24 minute miles)
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike is about 3.5-4 mph (15-17 minute miles)

HOW DO YOU PARTICIPATE?
Sign up with Meetup and RSVP Today! This also gets you on our email list to make you aware of upcoming events, hikes and walks. You will not be spammed. If you are, let me know. Spamming will not be tolerated.

WHY DO YOU NEED TO RSVP?
It's important to RSVP for these walks. When all the people have arrived for a walk that have RSVP'd, we leave... it might mean we leave early. If you didn't RSVP we are not going to wait for you. Plus, it's just a nice courtesy to the organizer and other participants. Please take the time to RSVP.

QUESTIONS?
Email me with any questions by using the "Contact Us" link on the left hand side bar of this meetup group page.

Hope to see you on a walk or hike soon!

Gary
SCO Organizer

title: Mindfulness Sunday Meditation: Cultivating Consciousness
description:
Meditate with a Monk in Sonoma County
Join us for a transformative workshop on mindfulness meditation and cultivating consciousness. Dive deep into the teachings of Theravada Buddhism, focusing on insight meditation to develop a clear understanding of the nature of the mind and consciousness. This workshop will include guided meditation sessions to help you strengthen your meditation practice and cultivate mindfulness in your daily life. Whether you are a beginner or an experienced meditator, this workshop offers a welcoming space to explore the depths of your own consciousness and enhance your spiritual journey. Come together with like-minded individuals to deepen your practice and connect with the wisdom of Theravada Buddhism, and provide an opportunity to deepen mindfulness, wisdom, and inner stillness.
Our sessions are led by Bhikkhunis closely associated with our Dhammadharini Sangha. Check out the [recording from the past event](https://youtube.com/live/s07U2kzWoWk?feature=share) on our YouTube channel.
You’re also welcome to join us in person at Dhammadharini Monastery, in the peaceful setting of our outdoor Dana Sala Pavilion
Register for this event on Dhammadharini's website to receive the address:
[https://www.dhammadharini.net/event-details/sunday-morning-guided-meditation-questions-2](https://www.dhammadharini.net/event-details/sunday-morning-guided-meditation-questions-2)

title: Tuesday Night Fitness Hike: 5+ Fast Miles, Downtown Petaluma and Western Hills
description:
"SONOMA COUNTY OUTDOORS"
WARNING: THE TUESDAY NIGHT FITNESS HIKE IS AN AEROBIC, FAST-PACED URBAN HIKE! WE TARGET A PACE OF 16-MINUTES PER MILE WITH ONLY BRIEF STOPS (TO REGROUP AS NEEDED). OUR SUMMER ROUTE INCLUDES THE HILLS IN HELEN PUTNAM PARK (740 FT. ELEVATION GAIN), AND OUR WINTER ROUTE EXPLORES THE WATER TANKS (690 FT. ELEVATION GAIN). IF YOU FIND YOU ARE HAVING DIFFICULTY KEEPING UP WITH THE LEADERS IN THIS GROUP, PLEASE USE THE OPT-OUT POINT AT THE FIRST MILE OF THE HIKE! ANOTHER OPTION IS OUR WEDNESDAY NIGHT WALK FOR A MORE MODERATE PACE. THANK YOU FOR HELPING ME KEEP THIS HIKE AN AEROBIC WORKOUT!

NOTE:
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike is posted on the SCO Calendar every week. Steve Tubbs is shown as the host each week but he might, or might not, show up to the event. This is, more often than not, a small group of regular, fit walkers who show up on time every Tuesday night to enjoy this rigorous walk. We leave promptly at 6:10 pm from the Kentucky Street entrance to the LanMart Building. So, if you don't see Steve on the Tuesday night you are there, you might see him on the next one.

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike, 5+ miles fast paced urban hike:

This Fitness Hike includes multiple steep uphill portions in Helen Putnam Park (during Daylight Savings Time), and at the Petaluma Water Tanks (after Daylight Savings Time ends).

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike:

* Warning! This is a FAST hike... a real workout!
* 5+ miles
* Meetup time 6:00 pm (We hike at 6:10 sharp)
* Difficulty is STRENUOUS!
* 90 minutes

This is a fast, evening Fitness Hike that starts downtown outside (on the sidewalk) of the LanMart Building (Brixx Restaurant, Heebe Jeebe) on Kentucky Street. We head west to Helen Putnam Park (or the Petaluma Water Tanks when DST ends) for some beautiful vistas before returning to our starting point on Kentucky Street. This hike is generally the same route and is focused primarily on fitness.

WHAT TO BRING:

* A good pair of walking/hiking shoes
* Water (you'll be glad you did)
* A fun attitude!

WHAT ABOUT THE DARKNESS?
Bring a SMALL flashlight. The sidewalks can be treacherous in west Petaluma, and you'll want to see those crags, cracks and upheavals in the concrete. Reflective clothing is also recommended so that vehicles can see you!

SO HOW FAST ARE WE WALKING?
The Wednesday Night Walk is about 2.5 mph (22 - 23 minute miles)
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike nearly 3.5 - 4.0 mph (we target a 16 minute mile, with multiple hills!)

HOW DO YOU PARTICIPATE?
Sign up with Meetup and RSVP Today! This also gets you on our email list to make you aware of upcoming events, hikes and walks.

WHY DO YOU NEED TO RSVP?

Please take the time to RSVP YES when you plan on attending an event. It is equally important to keep your RSVP up to date. If you've RSVP'd YES for an event, we are going to wait for you until the departure time. We leave promptly at 6:10 PM, so if you arrive late you can join us along the route. We typically hike the same route for each hike, and our focus is on aerobic exercise.

QUESTIONS?
Email me with any questions by using the "Contact Us" link on the left hand side bar of this meetup group page.

Hope to see you on a walk or hike soon!

SCO Organizers

title: The Sentence and book exchange
description:
Petaluma Book (And Brew) Club
Please bring 5 books you’d like to exchange. Any books you do not want returned may be left with us, and we will donate them to the Friends of the Library book sale.

The Sentence is a 2021 novel by Louise Erdrich, a ghost story set in a Minneapolis bookstore from November 2019 to November 2020, during the pandemic and George Floyd protests. It follows Tookie, a Native American woman recently released from prison, who is haunted by the ghost of an annoying customer, Flora, and must unravel the mystery while navigating personal challenges and a year of national turmoil. The book explores themes of grief, racism, addiction, and family, blending humor with profound reflection on what is owed to the living and the dead.

title: Wednesday Night Walk: Petaluma Downtown & Riverfront
description:
"SONOMA COUNTY OUTDOORS"
Wednesday Night Walk: Petaluma Downtown and Riverfront

* Want to walk for fitness and exercise?
* New to walking and want to build up stamina?
* Like a slower pace than our Tuesday Night Fitness Hike?
* Would walking with a committed group of walkers help you?

If you said yes to any of these, then the Wednesday Night Walk in Petaluma is for you. We start at Aqus Cafe and take in the West Side of town, including some of Downtown, the Waterfront and a few of the Historic home of old Petaluma. We walk about 3-1/2 to 4-1/2 miles depending on weather conditions and the pace of the group that night.

Afterward if you have the time, join us at Aqus Cafe for a bite to eat and some liquid refreshment before heading home. Aqus Cafe is a true gem of a gathering place, restaurant, coffee house, and live music venue. But it's the people on either side of the counter that make this place so special.

DETAILS:

* Meetup time: 6:00pm (we hike at 6:10 sharp)
* Meetup location: Aqus Cafe
* Distance: 3.5 to 4-1/2 miles
* Duration: 75-80 minutes
* Pace: Easy/Moderate (about 2.5-3 mph or 20-24 minute miles)
* Difficulty: Easy (if you've walked 3-4 miles recently)
* Hills: Mostly flat with a few small and easy to climb hills
* Optional After-Hike Gathering at Aqus Cafe

WHAT TO BRING:

* A good pair of walking shoes
* Water (you'll be glad you did)
* A fun attitude!

SO HOW FAST ARE WE WALKING?
The Wednesday Night Walk is about 2.5 - 3 mph (20-24 minute miles)
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike is about 3.5-4 mph (15-17 minute miles)

HOW DO YOU PARTICIPATE?
Sign up with Meetup and RSVP Today! This also gets you on our email list to make you aware of upcoming events, hikes and walks. You will not be spammed. If you are, let me know. Spamming will not be tolerated.

WHY DO YOU NEED TO RSVP?
It's important to RSVP for these walks. When all the people have arrived for a walk that have RSVP'd, we leave... it might mean we leave early. If you didn't RSVP we are not going to wait for you. Plus, it's just a nice courtesy to the organizer and other participants. Please take the time to RSVP.

QUESTIONS?
Email me with any questions by using the "Contact Us" link on the left hand side bar of this meetup group page.

Hope to see you on a walk or hike soon!

Gary
SCO Organizer

title: Happy Hour Crafts
description:
The Rebel Craft Collective
Wine + tasty snacks + your latest project and a friendly group of likeminded crafters... what better way to unwind? Come join us!

This is a relaxed, drop-in-friendly event. Come when you can, leave when you must. Newcomers and occasional-comers are always welcome!

**What do we mean by “crafts”?**
Whatever “craft” means to you! And whatever is portable enough to bring to a wine bar. Knitting, crochet, and other fiber arts are most common, but we have also warmly welcomed people who sketch, color, embroider, bead, and more. If your craft isn’t portable, we will happily ooh and aah over photos of your work-in-progress, or chat about your plans for your next project.

**Health & Safety**
Masks are very welcome, and nobody will pressure you to eat or drink. If the weather is nice, we will try to sit outside. If you aren’t eating/drinking during the event, please consider ordering some of La Dolce Vita’s delicious food to-go, in order to help support our gracious, long-time venue.

**Parking**
Parking in downtown Petaluma is free, but street parking has a strictly enforced 2 hour limit until 6pm. To park for longer, try the nearest garage:

* The Second Street Garage entrance is located on C Street between First and Second Streets. It's all day parking on every level and a short walk to La Dolce Vita.

**Ages**
It's a wine bar, so this event is for adult crafters (though you're certainly not required to drink wine!). We’re okay with babes-in-arms if you are, but this is not the right setting for wee crafters who are moving about on their own.

title: SUP Yoga on the Petaluma River
location: The Floathouse Petaluma, 50 Water Street, Petaluma, CA, 94952
description: SUNSET SUP Yoga on the Petaluma River, “Petaluma’s Longest Park” Step away from the rush and into the quiet of the Petaluma River for a peaceful SUP Yoga experience with The Floathouse Petaluma . And float into the sunset with us. Time to say goodbye to the week. Though we launch from the heart of downtown, the central turning basin offers a surprisingly serene setting—calm water, open sky, and a sense of ease that feels far removed from daily life. This all-levels, 90-minute session is designed for everyone: experienced yogis, seasoned paddle boarders, and complete beginners alike. We begin with a short, gentle paddle from the docks to get comfortable on your board (knees are always welcome). Once we reach our practice spot, we anchor together so tidal movement won’t interrupt your flow. From there, you’re invited to move, breathe, rest, or simply be—guided by an experienced instructor and supported by the shared rhythm of water and community. All equipment is provided, including extra-stable paddleboards measuring 34 inches wide and 11 feet long—much larger than a yoga mat and designed to help you feel grounded and secure on the water. title: Join us for Guided Buddhist Meditation and time for questions
description:
Meditate with a Monk in Sonoma County
New and experienced meditators are welcome. We will start with direct guidance to begin the practice and allow time to experience the silence of meditation on your own. There will be time at the end for your questions regarding meditation practice.

You may stay on for a potluck meal at 11:00 am. Welcome to bring a dish to share.

This is followed by Sutta Study program from 1:00 to 2:30 pm.

We meet outdoors in the Dhammadharini Monastery Garden in the Sala Pavillion, as long as conducive weather lasts.

Come in person, or register at [here](https://www.dhammadharini.net/event-details/sunday-morning-guided-meditation-questions-2) to attend online

title: Mindfulness Sunday Meditation: Cultivating Consciousness
description:
Meditate with a Monk in Sonoma County
Join us for a transformative workshop on mindfulness meditation and cultivating consciousness. Dive deep into the teachings of Theravada Buddhism, focusing on insight meditation to develop a clear understanding of the nature of the mind and consciousness. This workshop will include guided meditation sessions to help you strengthen your meditation practice and cultivate mindfulness in your daily life. Whether you are a beginner or an experienced meditator, this workshop offers a welcoming space to explore the depths of your own consciousness and enhance your spiritual journey. Come together with like-minded individuals to deepen your practice and connect with the wisdom of Theravada Buddhism, and provide an opportunity to deepen mindfulness, wisdom, and inner stillness.
Our sessions are led by Bhikkhunis closely associated with our Dhammadharini Sangha. Check out the [recording from the past event](https://youtube.com/live/s07U2kzWoWk?feature=share) on our YouTube channel.
You’re also welcome to join us in person at Dhammadharini Monastery, in the peaceful setting of our outdoor Dana Sala Pavilion
Register for this event on Dhammadharini's website to receive the address:
[https://www.dhammadharini.net/event-details/sunday-morning-guided-meditation-questions-2](https://www.dhammadharini.net/event-details/sunday-morning-guided-meditation-questions-2)
Check out the sangha website at

Cost per person includes tax and gratuity.

title: Tuesday Night Fitness Hike: 5+ Fast Miles, Downtown Petaluma and Western Hills
description:
"SONOMA COUNTY OUTDOORS"
WARNING: THE TUESDAY NIGHT FITNESS HIKE IS AN AEROBIC, FAST-PACED URBAN HIKE! WE TARGET A PACE OF 16-MINUTES PER MILE WITH ONLY BRIEF STOPS (TO REGROUP AS NEEDED). OUR SUMMER ROUTE INCLUDES THE HILLS IN HELEN PUTNAM PARK (740 FT. ELEVATION GAIN), AND OUR WINTER ROUTE EXPLORES THE WATER TANKS (690 FT. ELEVATION GAIN). IF YOU FIND YOU ARE HAVING DIFFICULTY KEEPING UP WITH THE LEADERS IN THIS GROUP, PLEASE USE THE OPT-OUT POINT AT THE FIRST MILE OF THE HIKE! ANOTHER OPTION IS OUR WEDNESDAY NIGHT WALK FOR A MORE MODERATE PACE. THANK YOU FOR HELPING ME KEEP THIS HIKE AN AEROBIC WORKOUT!

NOTE:
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike is posted on the SCO Calendar every week. Steve Tubbs is shown as the host each week but he might, or might not, show up to the event. This is, more often than not, a small group of regular, fit walkers who show up on time every Tuesday night to enjoy this rigorous walk. We leave promptly at 6:10 pm from the Kentucky Street entrance to the LanMart Building. So, if you don't see Steve on the Tuesday night you are there, you might see him on the next one.

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike, 5+ miles fast paced urban hike:

This Fitness Hike includes multiple steep uphill portions in Helen Putnam Park (during Daylight Savings Time), and at the Petaluma Water Tanks (after Daylight Savings Time ends).

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike:

* Warning! This is a FAST hike... a real workout!
* 5+ miles
* Meetup time 6:00 pm (We hike at 6:10 sharp)
* Difficulty is STRENUOUS!
* 90 minutes

This is a fast, evening Fitness Hike that starts downtown outside (on the sidewalk) of the LanMart Building (Brixx Restaurant, Heebe Jeebe) on Kentucky Street. We head west to Helen Putnam Park (or the Petaluma Water Tanks when DST ends) for some beautiful vistas before returning to our starting point on Kentucky Street. This hike is generally the same route and is focused primarily on fitness.

WHAT TO BRING:

* A good pair of walking/hiking shoes
* Water (you'll be glad you did)
* A fun attitude!

WHAT ABOUT THE DARKNESS?
Bring a SMALL flashlight. The sidewalks can be treacherous in west Petaluma, and you'll want to see those crags, cracks and upheavals in the concrete. Reflective clothing is also recommended so that vehicles can see you!

SO HOW FAST ARE WE WALKING?
The Wednesday Night Walk is about 2.5 mph (22 - 23 minute miles)
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike nearly 3.5 - 4.0 mph (we target a 16 minute mile, with multiple hills!)

HOW DO YOU PARTICIPATE?
Sign up with Meetup and RSVP Today! This also gets you on our email list to make you aware of upcoming events, hikes and walks.

WHY DO YOU NEED TO RSVP?

Please take the time to RSVP YES when you plan on attending an event. It is equally important to keep your RSVP up to date. If you've RSVP'd YES for an event, we are going to wait for you until the departure time. We leave promptly at 6:10 PM, so if you arrive late you can join us along the route. We typically hike the same route for each hike, and our focus is on aerobic exercise.

QUESTIONS?
Email me with any questions by using the "Contact Us" link on the left hand side bar of this meetup group page.

Hope to see you on a walk or hike soon!

SCO Organizers

title: Wednesday Night Walk: Petaluma Downtown & Riverfront
description:
"SONOMA COUNTY OUTDOORS"
Wednesday Night Walk: Petaluma Downtown and Riverfront

* Want to walk for fitness and exercise?
* New to walking and want to build up stamina?
* Like a slower pace than our Tuesday Night Fitness Hike?
* Would walking with a committed group of walkers help you?

If you said yes to any of these, then the Wednesday Night Walk in Petaluma is for you. We start at Aqus Cafe and take in the West Side of town, including some of Downtown, the Waterfront and a few of the Historic home of old Petaluma. We walk about 3-1/2 to 4-1/2 miles depending on weather conditions and the pace of the group that night.

Afterward if you have the time, join us at Aqus Cafe for a bite to eat and some liquid refreshment before heading home. Aqus Cafe is a true gem of a gathering place, restaurant, coffee house, and live music venue. But it's the people on either side of the counter that make this place so special.

DETAILS:

* Meetup time: 6:00pm (we hike at 6:10 sharp)
* Meetup location: Aqus Cafe
* Distance: 3.5 to 4-1/2 miles
* Duration: 75-80 minutes
* Pace: Easy/Moderate (about 2.5-3 mph or 20-24 minute miles)
* Difficulty: Easy (if you've walked 3-4 miles recently)
* Hills: Mostly flat with a few small and easy to climb hills
* Optional After-Hike Gathering at Aqus Cafe

WHAT TO BRING:

* A good pair of walking shoes
* Water (you'll be glad you did)
* A fun attitude!

SO HOW FAST ARE WE WALKING?
The Wednesday Night Walk is about 2.5 - 3 mph (20-24 minute miles)
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike is about 3.5-4 mph (15-17 minute miles)

HOW DO YOU PARTICIPATE?
Sign up with Meetup and RSVP Today! This also gets you on our email list to make you aware of upcoming events, hikes and walks. You will not be spammed. If you are, let me know. Spamming will not be tolerated.

WHY DO YOU NEED TO RSVP?
It's important to RSVP for these walks. When all the people have arrived for a walk that have RSVP'd, we leave... it might mean we leave early. If you didn't RSVP we are not going to wait for you. Plus, it's just a nice courtesy to the organizer and other participants. Please take the time to RSVP.

QUESTIONS?
Email me with any questions by using the "Contact Us" link on the left hand side bar of this meetup group page.

Hope to see you on a walk or hike soon!

Gary
SCO Organizer

Join us every other Thursday for a Jam like no other!

🎶 Scott Street Gin Jam at Griffo Distillery! 🎶

Join us EVERY 1st & 3rd Thursday at Griffo Distillery for the Scott Street Gin Jam! The Griffo jam is unlike any other and we want YOU to be a part of it! Doors open at 5pm, just in time to grab a cocktail, a seat, or load in your gear before the jam starts at 6pm!

All ages, all skill levels, and all genres welcome! Whether you play, sing, or just want to kick back with a cocktail and soak in the http://vibes...this http://vibes...this vibes...this is the best way to spend your Thursday!

PLUS, we've got "8 dolla holla cocktails" ALL NIGHT LONG!

Musicians: Bring your own instrument and amp if you have a preferred setup. Bring your pedals, http://horns...anything http://horns...anything horns...anything you've got or hop on our house drum kit, grab the mic and let's rock and roll!

Everyone else: Come grab a seat and watch the magic unfold! Bring your energy, your friends, your moves and get ready to dance your way into the weekend!

Hungry?! We've got you covered! Every 3rd Thursday our resident Grill Master, Ryan pulls his rig out to the patio, fires up the coals, and throws down for our Community BBQ & Potluck! Bring a side to share, something to throw on the grill, or your generosity for the tip jar - 'cuz wait till you try his http://ribs...and http://ribs...and ribs...and don't worry we've got veggie stuff too!

Come on out to make some music, shake your hips, sip on Griffo's ever-rotating cocktail menu, and keep the jam alive! See you at Thursdays Griffo Distillery! 🎸🥁🎷🍸 #ScottStreetGinJam #LiveMusic #GriffoDistillery

title: Theatre District Summer Concert Series – Josh Yenne
location: Theatre District,151 Petaluma Boulevard North, Petaluma, CA 94952, USA
description:
Theatre District is thrilled to announce the return of its Summer Concert Series for 2026. Beginning in June and running through September, the series features free live music every Friday from 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM in downtown Petaluma. The concert series brings together local talent and diverse musical styles, creating a vibrant community gathering in the heart of the Theatre District.

Josh Yenne https://joshyenne.com/ is performing from 6:00 to 8:00 in Theatre Square. We hope to see you there!

Josh Yenne is a versatile musician based in Petaluma, California, known for his expertise on the pedal steel guitar, guitar, and bass. With a career that spans various genres, including country, rock, blues, jazz, and bluegrass, Yenne has performed on stages around the world, from the Sydney Opera House to intimate house concerts in Petaluma. His solo acoustic shows often feature original songs that delve into historical American themes, blending elements of folk, ragtime, and Americana.

title: Upstream High Tide Paddle
location: The Floathouse Petaluma, 50 Water Street, Petaluma, CA, 94952
description: Upstream High Tide Paddle [High Tide: ~6.2 feet] When the tide rises, the river reveals a hidden world. Join The Floathouse crew for a gentle, guided paddle upstream on a high tide of over six feet , when the Petaluma River opens into its quieter, greener reaches. With extra water beneath us, we’re able to glide beyond the downtown channel and into a tranquil tidal slough—an ever-changing habitat rich with birdlife and natural beauty. Book your upstream adventure here. ($60/person includes gear, guide and nature’s awesomeness.) As we drift upstream, keep an eye out for great egrets, blue herons, snowy egrets, turtles basking along the banks , and the lush plant life that thrives where freshwater and tides meet. The pace is unhurried, the water is calm, and the experience is deeply grounding—many guests say they can feel their stress melt away within minutes. Along the way, our guide shares stories of the flora, fauna, and human history that have shaped this upper channel—from its ecological importance to its role in Petaluma’s past as a working river. You’ll come away with a deeper appreciation for how close this wild place is to the heart of downtown. ✨ Beginner-friendly 🚣 Sit-on-top kayaks 🌊 High tide access makes this route possible 🌿 A peaceful, nature-forward experience Come explore the Petaluma River at one of its most magical moments—when the tide is high, the river is deep, and the wild feels wonderfully close. location: Mackay Dressler Law Firm,422 Petaluma Boulevard North, Petaluma, CA 94952, USA, https://mackaydressler.com/workshops
description:
Creating your estate plan, whether it’s a living trust or a will, can be a daunting task. Estate planning addresses issues that are difficult to think about, such as death, incapacity, finances, and family dynamics. It can be easy to procrastinate, even though these issues may weigh heavily on your mind.

We invite you to attend one of our upcoming free webinars so you can take the first step toward having peace of mind by creating (or updating) your estate plan. This is an educational webinar, where we highlight some of the concerns that many families face and how an estate plan can help. The attorneys also break down how wills and trusts differ, and some of the common estate planning pitfalls and how to avoid them.

title: Tuesday Night Fitness Hike: 5+ Fast Miles, Downtown Petaluma and Western Hills
description:
"SONOMA COUNTY OUTDOORS"
WARNING: THE TUESDAY NIGHT FITNESS HIKE IS AN AEROBIC, FAST-PACED URBAN HIKE! WE TARGET A PACE OF 16-MINUTES PER MILE WITH ONLY BRIEF STOPS (TO REGROUP AS NEEDED). OUR SUMMER ROUTE INCLUDES THE HILLS IN HELEN PUTNAM PARK (740 FT. ELEVATION GAIN), AND OUR WINTER ROUTE EXPLORES THE WATER TANKS (690 FT. ELEVATION GAIN). IF YOU FIND YOU ARE HAVING DIFFICULTY KEEPING UP WITH THE LEADERS IN THIS GROUP, PLEASE USE THE OPT-OUT POINT AT THE FIRST MILE OF THE HIKE! ANOTHER OPTION IS OUR WEDNESDAY NIGHT WALK FOR A MORE MODERATE PACE. THANK YOU FOR HELPING ME KEEP THIS HIKE AN AEROBIC WORKOUT!

NOTE:
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike is posted on the SCO Calendar every week. Steve Tubbs is shown as the host each week but he might, or might not, show up to the event. This is, more often than not, a small group of regular, fit walkers who show up on time every Tuesday night to enjoy this rigorous walk. We leave promptly at 6:10 pm from the Kentucky Street entrance to the LanMart Building. So, if you don't see Steve on the Tuesday night you are there, you might see him on the next one.

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike, 5+ miles fast paced urban hike:

This Fitness Hike includes multiple steep uphill portions in Helen Putnam Park (during Daylight Savings Time), and at the Petaluma Water Tanks (after Daylight Savings Time ends).

Tuesday Night Fitness Hike:

* Warning! This is a FAST hike... a real workout!
* 5+ miles
* Meetup time 6:00 pm (We hike at 6:10 sharp)
* Difficulty is STRENUOUS!
* 90 minutes

This is a fast, evening Fitness Hike that starts downtown outside (on the sidewalk) of the LanMart Building (Brixx Restaurant, Heebe Jeebe) on Kentucky Street. We head west to Helen Putnam Park (or the Petaluma Water Tanks when DST ends) for some beautiful vistas before returning to our starting point on Kentucky Street. This hike is generally the same route and is focused primarily on fitness.

WHAT TO BRING:

* A good pair of walking/hiking shoes
* Water (you'll be glad you did)
* A fun attitude!

WHAT ABOUT THE DARKNESS?
Bring a SMALL flashlight. The sidewalks can be treacherous in west Petaluma, and you'll want to see those crags, cracks and upheavals in the concrete. Reflective clothing is also recommended so that vehicles can see you!

SO HOW FAST ARE WE WALKING?
The Wednesday Night Walk is about 2.5 mph (22 - 23 minute miles)
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike nearly 3.5 - 4.0 mph (we target a 16 minute mile, with multiple hills!)

HOW DO YOU PARTICIPATE?
Sign up with Meetup and RSVP Today! This also gets you on our email list to make you aware of upcoming events, hikes and walks.

WHY DO YOU NEED TO RSVP?

Please take the time to RSVP YES when you plan on attending an event. It is equally important to keep your RSVP up to date. If you've RSVP'd YES for an event, we are going to wait for you until the departure time. We leave promptly at 6:10 PM, so if you arrive late you can join us along the route. We typically hike the same route for each hike, and our focus is on aerobic exercise.

QUESTIONS?
Email me with any questions by using the "Contact Us" link on the left hand side bar of this meetup group page.

Hope to see you on a walk or hike soon!

SCO Organizers

title: Wednesday Night Walk: Petaluma Downtown & Riverfront
description:
"SONOMA COUNTY OUTDOORS"
Wednesday Night Walk: Petaluma Downtown and Riverfront

* Want to walk for fitness and exercise?
* New to walking and want to build up stamina?
* Like a slower pace than our Tuesday Night Fitness Hike?
* Would walking with a committed group of walkers help you?

If you said yes to any of these, then the Wednesday Night Walk in Petaluma is for you. We start at Aqus Cafe and take in the West Side of town, including some of Downtown, the Waterfront and a few of the Historic home of old Petaluma. We walk about 3-1/2 to 4-1/2 miles depending on weather conditions and the pace of the group that night.

Afterward if you have the time, join us at Aqus Cafe for a bite to eat and some liquid refreshment before heading home. Aqus Cafe is a true gem of a gathering place, restaurant, coffee house, and live music venue. But it's the people on either side of the counter that make this place so special.

DETAILS:

* Meetup time: 6:00pm (we hike at 6:10 sharp)
* Meetup location: Aqus Cafe
* Distance: 3.5 to 4-1/2 miles
* Duration: 75-80 minutes
* Pace: Easy/Moderate (about 2.5-3 mph or 20-24 minute miles)
* Difficulty: Easy (if you've walked 3-4 miles recently)
* Hills: Mostly flat with a few small and easy to climb hills
* Optional After-Hike Gathering at Aqus Cafe

WHAT TO BRING:

* A good pair of walking shoes
* Water (you'll be glad you did)
* A fun attitude!

SO HOW FAST ARE WE WALKING?
The Wednesday Night Walk is about 2.5 - 3 mph (20-24 minute miles)
The Tuesday Night Fitness Hike is about 3.5-4 mph (15-17 minute miles)

HOW DO YOU PARTICIPATE?
Sign up with Meetup and RSVP Today! This also gets you on our email list to make you aware of upcoming events, hikes and walks. You will not be spammed. If you are, let me know. Spamming will not be tolerated.

WHY DO YOU NEED TO RSVP?
It's important to RSVP for these walks. When all the people have arrived for a walk that have RSVP'd, we leave... it might mean we leave early. If you didn't RSVP we are not going to wait for you. Plus, it's just a nice courtesy to the organizer and other participants. Please take the time to RSVP.

QUESTIONS?
Email me with any questions by using the "Contact Us" link on the left hand side bar of this meetup group page.

Hope to see you on a walk or hike soon!

Gary
SCO Organizer

description:
Petaluma Urban Chat has launched The Vacancy Project, a bold new effort to tackle long-standing empty storefronts and underused lots in the heart of the city. At the center is an interactive, community-built Vacancy Map highlighting over 40 vacant properties within a half-mile of downtown—bringing visibility to an issue that’s been hiding in plain sight.

These spaces represent more than empty buildings. They mean lost opportunities for housing, local businesses, and a thriving downtown.

Now it’s time to take the next step.

* RSVP https://www.tickettailor.com/events/urbanchat/2174223 to join the conversation and help shape the future of downtown Petaluma.

Join us for a free community organizing meeting to turn insight into action. We’re bringing together residents, property owners, and local leaders to identify solutions, shape priorities, and begin building a shared roadmap to activate these spaces and bring new life to downtown Petaluma.

The event is free, and we ask that you RSVP https://www.tickettailor.com/events/urbanchat/2174223 in advance to be part of the conversation.

Happy Hour Crafts
description:
The Rebel Craft Collective
Wine + tasty snacks + your latest project and a friendly group of likeminded crafters... what better way to unwind? Come join us!

This is a relaxed, drop-in-friendly event. Come when you can, leave when you must. Newcomers and occasional-comers are always welcome!

**What do we mean by “crafts”?**
Whatever “craft” means to you! And whatever is portable enough to bring to a wine bar. Knitting, crochet, and other fiber arts are most common, but we have also warmly welcomed people who sketch, color, embroider, bead, and more. If your craft isn’t portable, we will happily ooh and aah over photos of your work-in-progress, or chat about your plans for your next project.

**Health & Safety**
Masks are very welcome, and nobody will pressure you to eat or drink. If the weather is nice, we will try to sit outside. If you aren’t eating/drinking during the event, please consider ordering some of La Dolce Vita’s delicious food to-go, in order to help support our gracious, long-time venue.

**Parking**
Parking in downtown Petaluma is free, but street parking has a strictly enforced 2 hour limit until 6pm. To park for longer, try the nearest garage:

* The Second Street Garage entrance is located on C Street between First and Second Streets. It's all day parking on every level and a short walk to La Dolce Vita.

**Ages**
It's a wine bar, so this event is for adult crafters (though you're certainly not required to drink wine!). We’re okay with babes-in-arms if you are, but this is not the right setting for wee crafters who are moving about on their own.

Blending elements of roots rock, folk, and country influences, the band has built a sound that feels both timeless and fresh, rooted in storytelling and musicianship. With a focus on strong songwriting and dynamic arrangements, the King Street Giants bring a lively and engaging presence to the stage, creating performances that resonate with a wide range of audiences. Their music captures the spirit of classic Americana while delivering a modern edge, making them a standout in today’s live music scene.

title: Convergence Ecstatic Dance
location: Kenilworth Teen Center,150 Fairgrounds Drive, Petaluma, CA 94952, USA
description:
Join Us for Convergence Ecstatic Dance!

Convergence is the Saturday night dance party you’ve been waiting for: the sultry vibe of low lights, plenty of room on the dance floor to move, no yelling to be heard over the music, no one spilling their drinks on the dance floor. Tune in to the music, your body, your emotions, the flow of the room, and let loose! This is your chance to connect with others and experience the joy of ecstatic dance in a chill, welcoming space. (There’s even a quiet room for stretching and resting.) No experience needed – just bring your energy and wear clothes you can move in. Don’t miss out on this fun, in-person event where the music and your spirit come together!

Convergence is a conscious dance experience centering Queer & BIPOC folks and welcoming allies. All ages, ethnicities, sexualities, gender expressions, and bodies welcome! No: alcohol, drugs, smoking, shoes, devices, talking on the dance floor.

Convergence is a spinoff from the original Ecstatic Dance electronic music. It has expanded to include music you know and love as well as new music. It spans across musical genres including hip hop, reggaeton, Afrobeats, House, and music from around the world that has a driving beat and makes your body move.

Let the rhythm show you how to move, sing along or vocalize if the spirit moves you, dance alone or with a consenting partner. Use this as a sacred time to get in touch with your emotions, release the ones that no longer serve you and welcoming in joy, levity, play, and peace.

“Ecstatic Dance is a freeform movement journey, held in a safe and sacred container, & facilitated by a professional DJ. It’s a place where we can be our unique selves, and also connected to a common source.” http://~ecstaticdance.org

So put on your comfy clothes, come alone or grab a friend, and get ready to sweat it out! Experience the wonder of moving together silently in community and using body language to communicate. Come early to help create the space and stay afterwards to talk to the friend you made on the dancefloor and help clean up. Community is built by participating fully together, and we’re excited to connect with you!

description: Learn to SUP: Build Skills. Find Flow. Ready to feel confident on a paddleboard? Our Learn to SUP class is a welcoming, two-hour introduction designed to help you paddle smarter — not harder — so you can truly enjoy your time on the water. Start your SUP journey here. For just $60 , you’ll learn from an ACA-certified (American Canoe Association) instructor in a small, supportive group of just 2–6 students . That means personalized attention, real feedback, and space to grow. We’ll cover: Proper stance and balance Efficient paddle technique Turning and maneuvering Launching and returning to the dock River awareness and safety basics Many people hop on a board and think they’re having fun — but they’re working twice as hard as they need to. This class unlocks the “aha” moments that make paddleboarding smoother, more efficient, and way more enjoyable. Held right in the heart of downtown Petaluma on the beautiful Petaluma River, this is your chance to build skills in a calm, supportive environment — and start feeling at home on the water. Bring a friend, learn together, and find your flow. All equipment included. Only 6 paddlers per class. title: Full Strawberry Moon Paddle/Pedal
location: The Floathouse Petaluma, 50 Water Street, Petaluma, CA 94952
description: 🍓 Strawberry Moon Paddle / Pedal Sunday, June 28, 2026 | 7:30–9:30 pm Join us for a warm summer evening on the Petaluma River under the Strawberry Moon , a name shared by many Native American cultures to mark the season of ripening fruit, blooming plants, and new life. This guided nighttime paddle in Hobie pedal kayaks is playful, easy, and perfect for lingering summer light and rising moonshine. Pedal along with your community as the river reflects the glow of early summer. June’s Full Moon is known by many names, each rooted in seasonal rhythms: Strawberry Moon — Algonquin, Ojibwe, Dakota, and Lakota peoples; the time when wild strawberries were ready to gather Berries Ripen Moon — Haida; marking the ripening of fruits Blooming Moon — Anishinaabe; celebrating peak flowering season Green Corn Moon — Cherokee; signaling the tending of crops Hoer Moon — Western Abenaki; associated with agricultural work Hot Moon — An 18th-century term recorded by Captain Jonathan Carver, reflecting early summer heat Birth Moon — Tlingit; the season when animals give birth Egg Laying Moon / Hatching Moon — Cree; marking new life emerging across the land These names remind us that this moon is about abundance, growth, and connection—perfect themes for an evening on the water. Event Details • Strawberry Moon Paddle / Pedal • Sunday, June 28, 2026 • 7:30–9:30 pm $60 per person includes: Hobie pedal kayak, experienced guide, PFD, all gear, and summer moonlight on the river. Book here! 🍓 Come play on the river at night and celebrate the season of berries, blooms, and long summer evenings. #block-653713b2782b5824cb96 { --stroke-style: none;--stroke-thickness: 6px; --tweak-text-block-background-color: initial; } #block-653713b2782b5824cb96 .sqs-html-content { --tweak-text-block-padding: 6% 6% 6% 6%; --tweak-text-block-padding: initial; } #block-653713b2782b5824cb96 { mix-blend-mode: var(--tweak-text-block-blend ); border-radius: var(--tweak-text-block-radius); } #block-653713b2782b5824cb96 { --tweak-text-block-radius: 0px 0px 0px 0px; } #block-653713b2782b5824cb96 { } @media screen and (max-width: 767px) { #block-653713b2782b5824cb96 { } } @media screen and (max-width: 767px) { #block-653713b2782b5824cb96 .sqs-html-content { } } @media screen and (max-width: 767px) { }

title: Scott Street Gin Jam: 1st & 3rd Thursdays EVERY Month
description:
Join us every other Thursday for a Jam like no other!

🎶 Scott Street Gin Jam at Griffo Distillery! 🎶

Join us EVERY 1st & 3rd Thursday at Griffo Distillery for the Scott Street Gin Jam! The Griffo jam is unlike any other and we want YOU to be a part of it! Doors open at 5pm, just in time to grab a cocktail, a seat, or load in your gear before the jam starts at 6pm!

All ages, all skill levels, and all genres welcome! Whether you play, sing, or just want to kick back with a cocktail and soak in the http://vibes...this http://vibes...this vibes...this is the best way to spend your Thursday!

PLUS, we've got "8 dolla holla cocktails" ALL NIGHT LONG!

Musicians: Bring your own instrument and amp if you have a preferred setup. Bring your pedals, http://horns...anything http://horns...anything horns...anything you've got or hop on our house drum kit, grab the mic and let's rock and roll!

Everyone else: Come grab a seat and watch the magic unfold! Bring your energy, your friends, your moves and get ready to dance your way into the weekend!

Hungry?! We've got you covered! Every 3rd Thursday our resident Grill Master, Ryan pulls his rig out to the patio, fires up the coals, and throws down for our Community BBQ & Potluck! Bring a side to share, something to throw on the grill, or your generosity for the tip jar - 'cuz wait till you try his http://ribs...and http://ribs...and ribs...and don't worry we've got veggie stuff too!

Come on out to make some music, shake your hips, sip on Griffo's ever-rotating cocktail menu, and keep the jam alive! See you at Thursdays Griffo Distillery! 🎸🥁🎷🍸 #ScottStreetGinJam #LiveMusic #GriffoDistillery

As featured in The Bohemian & Argus Courrier - Thank You Don Lewis & David Templeton!!

Please RSVP for this FREE, All Ages Event!

title: Free Community Yoga on The Floathouse Dock—First Fridays
location: The Floathouse Petaluma, 50 Water Street, Petaluma, CA, 94952
description: Free Community Yoga on The Floathouse Dock — First Fridays Fridays | 6:00–7:00 pm Join us for Free Community Yoga on The Floathouse Dock , an all-levels class that flows right along with Friday nights in downtown Petaluma. As the city eases into the evening—and sometimes live music drifts through the air—this outdoor practice invites you to move, stretch, and be part of the moment. Held on our dock—right on the Petaluma River—this class is relaxed, welcoming, and rooted in community. Each session is sponsored by a local small business, who’ll be on site after class to meet you and share in the evening. Free to attend, but registration is required due to limited space. Reserve your spot here. Bring your own mat if you have one (we’ll have a few extras), dress for the weather, and come solo or with a friend. description:
Nourish 108 Ayurveda & Yoga
Join me for 60 minutes of nourishing morning yoga in the serene Brooklyn Ballroom at the Hotel Petaluma. While I am here to offer a sequence of poses, this practice is yours to give your mind and body what it needs. Please bring your own yoga mat and any props you may need (strap, block, bolster, blanket) and arrive a few minutes early to get situated. Extra mats available for hotel guests.

All levels welcome!

Drop in is $18, class passes available, FREE for hotel guests. Sign up through the calendar at [www.nourish108.com/classes](www.nourish108.com/classes) or hotel front desk if you are a guest. Pay by credit/debit in advance or cash/Venmo on-site.

I look forward to seeing you on your mat!

title: SANDCASTLE DRAMA CAMP - Alice In Wonderland Theme
location: Polly Klaas Community Theater, 417 Western Avenue, Petaluma, CA, 94952, United States
description:
What: Kids explore the theater-making process through games and activities that build creativity, collaboration, and confidence. Each Sandcastle Drama Camp session explores a different story theme, the campers re-write the script as an ensemble to incorporate all their *original creative ideas for story, character, and design* resulting in a completely unique final play for performance each week.

Discounts & Flexible Pricing (sliding scale) available to all. Please complete a form and we will confirm your discount code via email https://forms.gle/QixDYDky7VUUhy6b9

Who: Kids ages 6-12

Program led by Sandcastle Theater Company's professional teaching artists
Approx. 16 students per weekly session (1:8 student/staff ratio)

Where: Polly Klaas Community Theater, 417 Western Ave. Petaluma, CA
When: Monday – Friday, 9am – 3pm

June 8 – 12 — make-your-own-play! Theme: The Princess & the Pea
July 6 – 10 — make-your-own-play! Theme: Alice in Wonderland
July 27 – 31 — make-your-own-play! Puss in Boots

Final Performances: Families and invited guests join us for a staged-reading/performance at 2:30pm on last day of the session.
Daily Schedule:

9am check-in/drop-off
9:30am warm-up games
10am session activities
10:30am snack
10:45am session activities
12pm lunch
12:30pm session activities
1:30pm recess
1:45pm session activities
3pm check-out/pick-up

Notes:

Kids bring their own lunch, water bottle, snacks

description:
The Rebel Craft Collective
Wine + tasty snacks + your latest project and a friendly group of likeminded crafters... what better way to unwind? Come join us!

This is a relaxed, drop-in-friendly event. Come when you can, leave when you must. Newcomers and occasional-comers are always welcome!

**What do we mean by “crafts”?**
Whatever “craft” means to you! And whatever is portable enough to bring to a wine bar. Knitting, crochet, and other fiber arts are most common, but we have also warmly welcomed people who sketch, color, embroider, bead, and more. If your craft isn’t portable, we will happily ooh and aah over photos of your work-in-progress, or chat about your plans for your next project.

**Health & Safety**
Masks are very welcome, and nobody will pressure you to eat or drink. If the weather is nice, we will try to sit outside. If you aren’t eating/drinking during the event, please consider ordering some of La Dolce Vita’s delicious food to-go, in order to help support our gracious, long-time venue.

**Parking**
Parking in downtown Petaluma is free, but street parking has a strictly enforced 2 hour limit until 6pm. To park for longer, try the nearest garage:

* The Second Street Garage entrance is located on C Street between First and Second Streets. It's all day parking on every level and a short walk to La Dolce Vita.

**Ages**
It's a wine bar, so this event is for adult crafters (though you're certainly not required to drink wine!). We’re okay with babes-in-arms if you are, but this is not the right setting for wee crafters who are moving about on their own.

description: Thursday Sunset Paddle & Party Ease into the evening with a relaxed paddle on the Petaluma River, followed by dockside snacks and river community time. We’ll always return to the dock about 30 minutes before sunset so everyone can relax, enjoy snacks on the dock, and soak in the riverfront atmosphere. Beginning in June and running through September, the series features free live music every Friday from 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM in downtown Petaluma. The concert series brings together local talent and diverse musical styles, creating a vibrant community gathering in the heart of the Theatre District.

Ariana LaMark https://www.facebook.com/lamarkariana/ is performing from 6:00 to 8:00 in Theatre Square. We hope to see you there!

Ariana LaMark is a Northern California–based singer, songwriter, and performer known for her smooth blend of contemporary R&B, pop, and soul influences. Drawing inspiration from honest storytelling and emotional experience, her music explores themes of love, growth, and self-reflection, delivered through warm, expressive vocals and modern production. With a sound that balances vulnerability and strength, Ariana LaMark creates performances that feel both intimate and powerful. Her stage presence is engaging and authentic, allowing audiences to connect deeply with her music while enjoying an energetic and polished live experience.

description: Learn to SUP: Build Skills. Find Flow. Ready to feel confident on a paddleboard? Our Learn to SUP class is a welcoming, two-hour introduction designed to help you paddle smarter — not harder — so you can truly enjoy your time on the water. Start your SUP journey here. For just $60 , you’ll learn from an ACA-certified (American Canoe Association) instructor in a small, supportive group of just 2–6 students . That means personalized attention, real feedback, and space to grow. We’ll cover: Proper stance and balance Efficient paddle technique Turning and maneuvering Launching and returning to the dock River awareness and safety basics Many people hop on a board and think they’re having fun — but they’re working twice as hard as they need to. This class unlocks the “aha” moments that make paddleboarding smoother, more efficient, and way more enjoyable. Held right in the heart of downtown Petaluma on the beautiful Petaluma River, this is your chance to build skills in a calm, supportive environment — and start feeling at home on the water. Bring a friend, learn together, and find your flow. All equipment included. Only 6 paddlers per class. title: Petaluma River History Paddle
location: The Floathouse Petaluma, 50 Water Street, Petaluma, CA, 94952
description: Petaluma River History Paddle The Petaluma River is the reason there’s a city here. Long before highways and railroads, this tidal waterway was the region’s saltwater highway —a working river that powered Petaluma’s rise and connected Sonoma County’s farms and businesses to San Francisco, the Gold Rush, and markets around the world. On this two-hour, gentle guided paddle , history comes alive through storytelling from multiple points of view. title: SUP Yoga on the Petaluma River
location: The Floathouse Petaluma, 50 Water Street, Petaluma, CA, 94952
description: SUP Yoga on the Petaluma River, “Petaluma’s Longest Park” Step away from the rush and into the quiet of the Petaluma River for a peaceful SUP Yoga experience with The Floathouse Petaluma . Though we launch from the heart of downtown, the central turning basin offers a surprisingly serene setting—calm water, open sky, and a sense of ease that feels far removed from daily life. This all-levels, 90-minute session is designed for everyone: experienced yogis, seasoned paddle boarders, and complete beginners alike. We begin with a short, gentle paddle from the docks to get comfortable on your board (knees are always welcome). Once we reach our practice spot, we anchor together so tidal movement won’t interrupt your flow. From there, you’re invited to move, breathe, rest, or simply be—guided by an experienced instructor and supported by the shared rhythm of water and community. All equipment is provided, including extra-stable paddleboards measuring 34 inches wide and 11 feet long—much larger than a yoga mat and designed to help you feel grounded and secure on the water. Come as you are. Choose your own level of effort. Flow with the river and the people around you. It’s YOUR river. Come out and play. $50/person, includes all gear, instruction, and quality time on the water. title: Theatre District Summer Concert Series – Steve Pile Band
location: Theatre District,151 Petaluma Boulevard North, Petaluma, CA 94952, USA
description:
Theatre District is thrilled to announce the return of its Summer Concert Series for 2026. Beginning in June and running through September, the series features free live music every Friday from 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM in downtown Petaluma. The concert series brings together local talent and diverse musical styles, creating a vibrant community gathering in the heart of the Theatre District.

Steve Pile Band https://stevepile.com/ is performing from 6:00 to 8:00 in Theatre Square. We hope to see you there!

The Steve Pile Band, a fixture in the Petaluma music scene, offers a unique blend of delta blues, country, African rhythms, and jam band influences. Founded by Steve Pile, a singer-songwriter and guitarist, the band has developed a distinctive sound that combines the traditional with the eclectic. Pile’s musical journey has taken him from Alaska to Austin and even West Africa, where he incorporated local musical elements into his style. Known for their dynamic performances, the Steve Pile Band has been a staple at various venues across Northern California, consistently drawing audiences with their compelling mix of original tunes and energetic jams .

description: Intermediate SUP: Refine Skills. Expand Horizons. Ready for what’s next? Our Intermediate SUP lessons are designed for paddlers who have completed Learn to SUP (or have equivalent experience with at least 10+ hours on the water) and are ready to deepen their skills, efficiency, and confidence. This is where paddleboarding starts to feel powerful. For $85 , you’ll spend two focused hours on the Petaluma River with an ACA-certified instructor , in an intentionally small group of no more than 5 students . Expect personalized coaching, detailed feedback, and real skill development. We’ll refine and build upon the fundamentals: A stronger, more efficient forward stroke Advanced turning techniques Confident footwork and stance transitions Improved balance and stability Understanding water dynamics and river movement Paddling faster, straighter, and with less effort As your technique improves, new possibilities open — longer paddles, windier conditions, higher tides, touring beyond the basics, and exploring new waterways with confidence. Held in the heart of downtown Petaluma on the Petaluma River, this class is your next step toward truly feeling at home on your board. Only 5 paddlers per session. Personalized attention. Meaningful progression. Ready to paddle farther, smoother, and with real confidence? Take the next step. title: Upstream High Tide Paddle
location: The Floathouse Petaluma, 50 Water Street, Petaluma, CA, 94952
description: Sunset Upstream High Tide Paddle [High Tide: ~6.5 feet] When the tide rises, the river reveals a hidden world. Join The Floathouse crew for a gentle, guided paddle upstream on a high tide of 6.5 feet , when the Petaluma River opens into its quieter, greener reaches. With extra water beneath us, we’re able to glide beyond the downtown channel and into a tranquil tidal slough—an ever-changing habitat rich with birdlife and natural beauty. Book your upstream adventure here. ($60/person includes gear, guide and nature’s awesomeness.) As we drift upstream, keep an eye out for great egrets, blue herons, snowy egrets, turtles basking along the banks , and the lush plant life that thrives where freshwater and tides meet. The pace is unhurried, the water is calm, and the experience is deeply grounding—many guests say they can feel their stress melt away within minutes. Along the way, our guide shares stories of the flora, fauna, and human history that have shaped this upper channel—from its ecological importance to its role in Petaluma’s past as a working river. You’ll come away with a deeper appreciation for how close this wild place is to the heart of downtown. ✨ Beginner-friendly 🚣 Sit-on-top kayaks 🌊 High tide access makes this route possible 🌿 A peaceful, nature-forward experience Come explore the Petaluma River at one of its most magical moments—when the tide is high, the river is deep, and the wild feels wonderfully close. title: Happy Hour Crafts
description:
The Rebel Craft Collective
Wine + tasty snacks + your latest project and a friendly group of likeminded crafters... what better way to unwind? Come join us!

This is a relaxed, drop-in-friendly event. Come when you can, leave when you must. Newcomers and occasional-comers are always welcome!

**What do we mean by “crafts”?**
Whatever “craft” means to you! And whatever is portable enough to bring to a wine bar. Knitting, crochet, and other fiber arts are most common, but we have also warmly welcomed people who sketch, color, embroider, bead, and more. If your craft isn’t portable, we will happily ooh and aah over photos of your work-in-progress, or chat about your plans for your next project.

**Health & Safety**
Masks are very welcome, and nobody will pressure you to eat or drink. If the weather is nice, we will try to sit outside. If you aren’t eating/drinking during the event, please consider ordering some of La Dolce Vita’s delicious food to-go, in order to help support our gracious, long-time venue.

**Parking**
Parking in downtown Petaluma is free, but street parking has a strictly enforced 2 hour limit until 6pm. To park for longer, try the nearest garage:

* The Second Street Garage entrance is located on C Street between First and Second Streets. It's all day parking on every level and a short walk to La Dolce Vita.

**Ages**
It's a wine bar, so this event is for adult crafters (though you're certainly not required to drink wine!). We’re okay with babes-in-arms if you are, but this is not the right setting for wee crafters who are moving about on their own.

title: "Paddle The Petaluma: Turn to The River" Guided Kayak Tour
location: The Floathouse Petaluma,50 Water Street, Petaluma, CA 94952, USA
description:
Paddle the Petaluma: Turn to The River is a relaxed, beginner-friendly guided kayak tour exploring the past, present, and future of Petaluma’s historic waterway. Launching right from downtown at The Floathouse Petaluma https://www.thefloathousepetaluma.org?utm_source=chatgpt.com , this Sonoma County Signature Experience spends about 90 minutes on the water in stable sit-on-top kayaks, traveling a gentle mile-and-a-half route through “Petaluma’s Longest Park.”

Along the way, you’ll raft up at docks around town, fascinating landmarks, and riverfront gathering spaces to hear stories about how this Gold Rush-era “saltwater highway” helped shape Petaluma—and how today’s community is continuing to reinvent and reconnect with the river. This isn’t just a history tour. You’ll also learn about the people, businesses, artists, nonprofits, and river advocates helping shape the waterway’s future right now.

Everything is included in the $75 experience: kayak, gear, knowledgeable local guides, insider river stories, and post-paddle perks at nearby businesses. Finish with plenty of time for brunch, coffee, shopping, or simply hanging out downtown by the water. No experience necessary.

Note: The Floathouse Petaluma is a nonprofit project dedicated to “putting butts in boats and smiles on faces” by offering year-round easy access to the Petaluma River in and on people-powered water craft through rentals, events, classes, lessons and summer camps.

title: Turn to The River: A Guided Paddle through The Past, Present, & Future of an Iconic Sonoma County Waterway
location: The Floathouse Petaluma, 50 Water Street, Petaluma, CA 94952
description: Turn to The River: a guided paddle tour The future is NOW for the Petaluma River, the historic Sonoma County waterway credited for the birth, growth, and lasting relevance of the charming Bay Area city of Petaluma, California. Just 40 miles north of San Francisco, let us take you on a journey through the past, present, and future of the long & winding “saltwater highway” that brought Petaluma to life and continues to support how we live and play today. This tidal slough—the Petaluma River —inspired generations of immigrants to conceive of industrial and pastoral innovations that shaped the history of the entire San Francisco Bay area and beyond. From the days of the Gold Rush to the present moment, the Petaluma River has beckoned miners and farmers, industrialists and solopreneurs, visionaries and ecologists to imagine new ways of interacting with this place. It remains an ever-changing connector between wetlands and city, land and water, past and future. Book your seat today on this fascinating guided kayak tour —$75 per person includes all gear, an experienced guide, and post-paddle perks at local businesses. title: Convergence Ecstatic Dance
location: Kenilworth Teen Center,150 Fairgrounds Drive, Petaluma, CA 94952, USA
description:
Join Us for Convergence Ecstatic Dance!

Convergence is the Saturday night dance party you’ve been waiting for: the sultry vibe of low lights, plenty of room on the dance floor to move, no yelling to be heard over the music, no one spilling their drinks on the dance floor. Tune in to the music, your body, your emotions, the flow of the room, and let loose! This is your chance to connect with others and experience the joy of ecstatic dance in a chill, welcoming space. (There’s even a quiet room for stretching and resting.) No experience needed – just bring your energy and wear clothes you can move in. Don’t miss out on this fun, in-person event where the music and your spirit come together!

Convergence is a conscious dance experience centering Queer & BIPOC folks and welcoming allies. All ages, ethnicities, sexualities, gender expressions, and bodies welcome! No: alcohol, drugs, smoking, shoes, devices, talking on the dance floor.

Convergence is a spinoff from the original Ecstatic Dance electronic music. It has expanded to include music you know and love as well as new music. It spans across musical genres including hip hop, reggaeton, Afrobeats, House, and music from around the world that has a driving beat and makes your body move.

Let the rhythm show you how to move, sing along or vocalize if the spirit moves you, dance alone or with a consenting partner. Use this as a sacred time to get in touch with your emotions, release the ones that no longer serve you and welcoming in joy, levity, play, and peace.

“Ecstatic Dance is a freeform movement journey, held in a safe and sacred container, & facilitated by a professional DJ. It’s a place where we can be our unique selves, and also connected to a common source.” http://~ecstaticdance.org

So put on your comfy clothes, come alone or grab a friend, and get ready to sweat it out! Experience the wonder of moving together silently in community and using body language to communicate. Come early to help create the space and stay afterwards to talk to the friend you made on the dancefloor and help clean up. Community is built by participating fully together, and we’re excited to connect with you!
